COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
CLR No. 11 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Siddhant Manral, learned counsel for
the revisionist.
2. Mr. Sagar Kothari, learned counsel for the
respondent.
3. By the instant revision the revisionist is
assailing the order passed by the Trial Court,
whereby, the Trial Court passed an order to
proceed ex parte. In addition to this, the
revisionist is also challenging the order dated
26.07.2024, whereby on an application of the
plaintiff the written statement filed by the
defendants was also returned.
4. On the previous occasion, taking into
consideration that the dispute is in between the
two real brothers the attempts were made for their
amicable settlement through their respective
counsel, but no amicable settlement could be
arrived in between the parties. In such an
eventuality, this court is of the view that the
dispute in between both the brothers has to be
decided by the Trial Court.
5. Since, the Trial Court passed an order to
proceed exparte against the revisionist, who is the
defendant in the suit, therefore, for substantial
justice particularly when both the parties are real
brother could not arrive for their amicable
settlement, the orders impugned are set aside and
the matter is remanded back to the Trial Court
with the direction that the Trial Court expedite the
trial in accordance with law positively within
three months from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.
6. It is made clear since the order passed by the
Trial Court by which the written statement was
returned back to the defendant is set aside, the
written statement shall be treated to be part of the
Trial Court proceeding.
